data.title: Publishing the band before the interview becomes a duty in the EU (Directive 2023/970, Art. 5)
data.summary: EU law requires employers to give applicants the initial pay or its range for the advertised position, set on objective and gender-neutral criteria, "in a manner such as to ensure an informed and transparent negotiation on pay, such as in a published job vacancy notice, prior to the job interview or otherwise", and to state the applicable collective agreement where there is one. It also forbids asking an applicant about their pay history in current or previous employment, and requires vacancy notices and job titles to be gender-neutral. The directive is being transposed into national law across Member States, and the reporting duties in Article 9 begin on 7 June 2027 for the largest employers. It fixes when a number must be disclosed, not that the number cannot move afterwards.
data.citation: Directive (EU) 2023/970 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 10 May 2023, Article 5 (Pay transparency prior to employment).
